findings.summary: Android is a Linux-based operating system developed by Google, primarily for smartphones and tablets, distributed as the Android Open Source Project (AOSP) under Apache-2.0 and GPL-2.0-only licenses. Most devices run a proprietary open-core version including Google Mobile Services (GMS). The system supports 64-bit ARM and x86-64, and 32-bit ARMv7 and x86 ABIs. Applications are packaged as APKs and distributed via stores such as Google Play or third-party alternatives. The kernel is monolithic Linux, with a userland of Bionic libc, mksh, and Toybox. The UI is graphical and multi-touch. Updates are delivered over-the-air.

mechanisms.title: Application sandboxing and APK distribution
mechanisms.explanation: Android packages software as APK files, which are installed and executed within a sandboxed environment. The platform enforces permission-based access control, and most devices rely on Google Play or vendor stores for distribution, though AOSP allows third-party stores and open-source alternatives.

mechanisms.title: Linux kernel and Bionic userland
mechanisms.explanation: The operating system runs a monolithic Linux kernel paired with a Bionic libc implementation, mksh shell, and Toybox utilities. This combination provides the core system services, memory management, and hardware abstraction for the graphical multi-touch interface.
